title: lore agent context: one SECTION can appear twice in omittedSections with two different reasons
description:
Filed 2026-10-14 from the LCLI-722 Piece B Stage 1 review (opum-ai/lore-cli#600) as its own observation, not folded into that PR.

FACT. budgets.taskEvidence.omittedSections is built by iterating every candidate of every declared source. When a source is large enough to be partitioned AND a part then exceeds the split threshold, buildSourceCandidates (src/core/agent-context.ts, via splitTopLevelBlocks) splits that part into top-level blocks, and every block KEEPS its parent breadcrumb. Two such blocks then appear as two entries with the SAME reference and section and DIFFERENT reason.

MEASURED. A bundle whose ranked document is one H1 with three H2 sections, at max_tokens 400 — so the split threshold min(2000, maxTokens/4) is 100 tokens — reports "Ranked > Alpha = scored-zero" beside "Ranked > Alpha = cut-by-max-tokens": the heading block shares no term with the task and scores zero, while the paragraph block beneath it matches and the pack budget cuts it. Reproduced in the Piece B session against a temp bundle through the real compiler.

WHY IT READS WRONG. The report exists to say, per SECTION, why that section is absent (LCLI-722 AC4, DEC-194 (11)). Naming one heading twice, once as never-eligible and once as cut by a ceiling, reads as self-contradictory, and a reader cannot tell from the report that these are two different candidates of one section.

NOT SEEN in the four real role profiles: they measure at budgets where the threshold is high enough that no part is block-split. Of the AC4 acceptance tests, only the one at max_tokens 400 shows it.

FIX SHAPE IS A DESIGN CALL, deliberately not made here: disambiguate a block-level candidate identity (a part index, an offset, or a flag marking a block-level entry), or report block-level candidates under their own label. Referred rather than chosen.

Evidence: opum-ai/lore-cli#600 head 327498c5b4edea4a5d5ac1ed6c735245bb24a8ca, where the observation was made and reported to the orchestrator.
